headline: CM Maryam launches Rs2 trillion PIVOT initiative to boost industry, exports
description: The roadmap targets $6.8 billion in incremental exports, 162,000 new direct jobs and support for over one million families.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Friday officially launched the Punjab Innovation for Value, Opportunity and Transformation (PIVOT) Plan 2026-29 – around Rs2 trillion economic strategy aimed at positioning Punjab as an export-led industrial hub.

The roadmap targets $6.8 billion in incremental exports, 162,000 new direct jobs and support for over one million families.

Speaking at the launch, the chief minister said: “Punjab is ready to move towards a new model of economic growth, driven by industry, innovation, value addition and exports. Our objective is to create an environment where businesses can invest with confidence, industries can expand and our people can access better employment and livelihood opportunities.”

She said: “PIVOT will not remain a document of targets and commitments. Its implementation will be tracked, its progress measured and its results assessed. Every initiative must translate into real investment, stronger businesses, more exports and better opportunities for the people of Punjab.”

The three-year plan envisages $6.8bn exports, 162,000 direct jobs

She said her message to investors and industrialists across Pakistan and around the world was clear --- “Punjab welcomes your investment. We want to work with you, facilitate your businesses and create the conditions in which enterprise can grow. Government will facilitate, industry will lead.”

The chief minister said sustainable growth required private investment, a strong industrial base and a partnership in which the public sector enables the private sector to innovate, produce and compete. “PIVOT is designed to turn that partnership into measurable economic progress. Our industries must not be limited to producing more; they must produce better, add greater value and compete in international markets. We want Punjab’s manufacturers to have access to modern technology, reliable energy solutions, quality infrastructure and the financing they need to expand their businesses and exports,” she said and added young people must be prepared for the jobs of tomorrow. Skills development must respond to the actual needs of industry and the changing demands of the economy as training leads to employment, entrepreneurship and better livelihoods.

“Investors should spend their time building businesses, creating jobs and expanding production—not navigating unnecessary administrative hurdles. We are working to make government services simpler, more accessible and more transparent.”

The launch brought together leading corporate figures, economic policymakers, international development agencies and diplomats. Prominent businessmen Mian Mansha, Arif Habib, Fawad Mukhtar, Zaid Bashir and Osman Khalid Waheed were among those who attended the event, signalling private sector’s engagement with the initiative.

State Bank of Pakistan Governor Jameel Ahmad, heads of major commercial banks and financial institutions, members of the diplomatic corps and representatives of key international development partners, including the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and UN also participated in the launch.

Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb, Punjab Chief Secretary Zahid Akhtar Zaman, provincial cabinet ministers and administrative secretaries were also present. A primary pillar of the PIVOT framework is the Strategic Trade Enhancement Programme (STEP), supported by a newly introduced digital portal. Under this mechanism, the government envisages Rs300 billion in concessional financing at rates ranging between zero and five per cent for eligible commercial categories, giving businesses access to lower-cost capital for expansion, subject to programme terms and conditions.

This financing structure forms part of an overall investment framework combining Rs1,089bn in public investment with a target of Rs906bn in private-sector investment. The plan directs Rs753.7bn towards strengthening industrial output, encouraging value addition and building long-term export competitiveness.

To address operational costs and energy challenges, the government has earmarked Rs50bn for solar power installations and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). An additional Rs50bn has been allocated for machinery duty reimbursements to incentivise manufacturers to upgrade factories, adopt advanced technology and meet international quality standards.

The programme focuses on key manufacturing value chains, including garments and textiles, sports goods, leather and footwear, surgical instruments, pharmaceuticals, fans, cutlery, steel and ceramics.

Modern testing laboratories, certification facilities and plug-and-play industrial infrastructure are also envisaged to help businesses meet international compliance requirements and access export markets.

To move agriculture beyond raw commodity production towards higher-value processing, PIVOT includes four specialised agro-processing parks, one each in Sargodha, Khanewal, Okara and Bhakkar.

The plan also extends to tourism, digital services and workforce development. To improve the business environment, PIVOT introduces regulatory and administrative reforms aimed at simplifying commercial operations and attracting long-term investment.

Through the E-Biz digital initiative, the provincial government aims to digitise 300 public administrative services to make business processes more accessible and transparent.

The programme also envisages bringing 2,000 firms onto e-commerce platforms, alongside modernised labour laws, public-private partnership reforms and approved schemes for state land leases across nine productive economic sectors.

Execution and accountability are embedded through a central governance model led by a PIVOT Board, presided over by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb on behalf of the chief minister. Operational coordination will be handled by a dedicated PIVOT Secretariat in the Planning and Development Department, alongside a PIVOT cell within the chief secretary’s office. Deputy commissioners will serve as district-level focal persons.

State Bank Governor Jameel Ahmed highlighted major financial milestones, saying SME financing surged 61pc to Rs1.1 trillion by June 2026, serving nearly 326,000 borrowers. He outlined ambitious targets to expand this reach to Rs2 trillion and 775,000 borrowers by fiscal year 2028.

He also noted strong momentum in specialised agricultural schemes like Zarkhez and rapid growth in housing finance. He reaffirmed the central bank’s commitment to driving sustainable economic development across Punjab.

Mian Muhammad Mansha, chairman of Nishat Group and MCB Bank, pointed to seamless building permissions and praised significant police reforms.

“Drivers and locals now report a professional, well-compensated police force operating without street-level corruption,” he said.

American Business Forum President Osman Khalid Waheed hailed the PIVOT initiative as the province’s most ambitious economic expansion plan. He hoped the plan would boost global competitiveness across agriculture, manufacturing, technology, and healthcare, while generating over 200,000 skilled jobs through competitive industrial clusters.

Gul Ahmed Textiles Director Ziad Bashir highlighted six key drivers of the province’s competitive edge: security, motorway connectivity, reliable energy, digital land records, streamlined regulatory approvals, and a 120-million-strong market larger than any EU nation.

Bashir commended the chief minister for delivering on promises and fostering an investor-friendly environment. Pledging full support on behalf of the Pakistan Business Council, he affirmed that Punjab would not walk its ambitious economic growth path alone.

Arif Habib Group Chairman Arif Habib commended Punjab’s strategic focus on construction and progress tracking via digital dashboards. Habib credited the chief minister’s use of privatised PIA to inspire improvements in the airline’s service and punctuality.

Fatima Group Chairman Fawad Mukhtar expressed confidence that the business community would fully support the initiative, lauding the chief minister’s thorough engagement and declared that this venture represents the economic future of both Punjab and Pakistan.

Published in Dawn, October 31st, 2026

headline: Over 1,460 illegal medical centres sealed in 3 months in KP
description: The report states that 610 new medical centres were registered during the last three months, bringing the total number of registered healthcare facilities in the province to 22,910.
author: APP
article_text:
PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Healthcare Commission has sealed 1,465 illegal medical centres across the province during the last three months, according to its latest performance report on Friday.

The report revealed that the commission inspected 6,673 medical facilities across the province during the period. Notices seeking explanations were also issued to 2,668 centres over various violations.

According to the commission’s spokesperson, Azam Rehman, measures were also taken to improve the registration and licensing of healthcare facilities and address public complaints.

The report stated that 610 new medical centres were registered during the last three months, bringing the total number of registered healthcare facilities in the province to 22,910.

Meanwhile, 52 medical centres were granted full licences during the same period, taking the total number of fully licensed facilities since 2023 to 326.

The commission also received 267 public complaints regarding healthcare services, of which 203 were resolved.

The commission’s director of operations, Arsalan Ahmed Khan, said that the registration and licensing process aims to ensure the provision of quality healthcare services to the public.

Published in Dawn, October 31st, 2026

headline: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
description: The approval comes after weeks of complaints by Ukrainian authorities that its supplies of the interceptor missiles were dwindling.
author: AFP
article_text:
The Trump administration on Friday green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, the State Department said, but the Ukrainian president warned deliveries could take years.

The approval, which goes to Congress for review, comes after weeks of complaints by Ukrainian authorities that its supplies of the interceptor missiles were dwindling.

“The proposed sale will improve Ukraine’s capability to meet current and future threats by improving its integrated air and missile defense capabilities,” the department said in a statement.

The statement did not provide an estimate for when the weapons could be delivered to Ukraine.

But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said late Friday in a post on X that “deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS.”

“We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors,” Zelensky said, using an acronym for the weapons.

The Ukrainian leader suggested that the US and European allies could give his country missiles they have stockpiled now, which would later be replenished by this new purchase.

Patriot missiles are among the most important weapons Ukraine has to intercept Russian drones and missiles.

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe,” the State Department said.

US-Ukraine tensions spiked earlier this month after Washington struck a diesel fuel deal with Russia. Ukraine also said that the US was slowing its access to satellite internet services and had stopped some intelligence sharing.

Tensions eased after Zelensky held talks with US envoys in Oslo on October 20.

The State Department said the weapons sale would be paid for with by donations from Ukraine’s allies but not with US funds.

headline: Iran says 4th oil tanker hit mine, caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said Friday that a fourth oil tanker had struck a mine and...
article_text:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said Friday that a fourth oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire while attempting to pass through an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, IRNA reports.

The navy’s public relations office said the supertanker, carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil, ignored repeated radio warnings against using the southern passage through the strategic waterway.

The vessel was struck by a mine, triggering a powerful explosion and leaving it burning, according to the statement.

headline: This upcoming indie horror game inspired by Lahore's smog turns Pakistani trauma into treasure
description: Fogbound features a poisonous, mind-eroding fog spreading through a 3D-modelled Lahore — inspired by the developer watching smog worsen year after year.
author: Nazish Talati
article_text:
Every year, Lahore is choked by a smog season worse than the last one, points out student and independent video game developer Ibrahim Hisham. This is his inspiration for Fogbound — a short psychological horror game slated to release at the end of this year under his studio Minidevs — which features a poisonous, mind-eroding fog spreading through a 3D-modelled Lahore.

The game is a story-based walking simulator that has the player assume the role of Riaz, a member of the Air Quality Task Force in the quarantined city. As Riaz, you explore different pockets of the city, decontaminating zones and placing monitors to keep things running as best as possible. The fog, meanwhile, turns people into ‘sayahs’ — literally shadows of their former selves — and as Lahore is fully locked down, trying to get you and your partner Amara out is a bureaucratic nightmare of its own.

Despite being only 18 years old, this is not the first game Hisham has published. In fact, the developer has been creating games since before he hit double digits, including arcade shooter Pointblank on Steam and several game jam creations available on Itch.io. While all of them are entirely different in style, concept and genre, this one is described as “mostly interactive fiction”, akin to a walking simulator — there will be “light combat” and puzzle elements, but the main focus is on telling a story through dialogue, exploration and a linear narrative of about one and a half to two hours.

Hisham told Dawn that the toxic fog is heavily based on his experience growing up in Lahore, where he has watched the air quality decline year after year.

“I think grade 4 or 5 was the first time I remember it was something we talked about in our morning assemblies,” he recalled. “After that it just got worse … We had to start wearing masks around that season.”

In 2024, his school shut down for about two weeks due to hazardous air quality, which was where the seed was planted for the game.

“I think that also gave me a bunch of free time to think about the situation a little more,” he added jokingly. “And so, just sort of extrapolating that into … a horror idea for an imagined future where it just goes completely crazy.”

Although the game is not quite rooted in realism, it promises splashes of reality in the themes it explores. For example, the central tension of the story revolves around Amara, Riaz’s partner whom he brought to Lahore before the quarantine, and the resulting conflict between the two as he tries to get her back out.

The specificity of the developer’s experience with Lahore’s worsening smog is why the game is firmly rooted in the city itself, instead of just inspired by it. That said, it isn’t intended to be a game exclusively ‘for Pakistanis’, and the appeal of the premise extends beyond just finding new local talent.

“I would say it’s more of a storyline that transcends,” he said. “It’s grounded in that culture and that setting, but the story itself revolves around a bunch of themes like dissociation, guilt — something that would be applicable to a wider audience.

“I don’t think I could imagine this story that I’ve thought out happening outside of Pakistan, because the entire smog conflict is something that I wanted it to be rooted in,” he added.

“My idea with this in terms of appeal is that I want Pakistanis to feel represented, but I don’t want the story to just remain confined to something that only a Pakistani were to enjoy.”

Still, the game’s Pakistani roots and setting will be felt by players in another way: while the upcoming release of Fogbound will be in English, Hisham is planning to roll out a roman Urdu translation later so that it can reach the wider subcontinent. (Right-to-left or RTL text, for languages such as Urdu and Arabic, is a notoriously difficult facet of game localisation, so an Urdu-script translation remains off the table for now.)

Fogbound is created by a team of three. The art — featuring low-poly models deliberately designed to evoke old PlayStation games and a 3D-modelled city of Lahore — is all handled by one artist, while the music consists of 20-30 “dark ambient” tracks composed by a musician in Russia who was recruited to the project through Discord. The rest of it is entirely spearheaded and executed by Hisham.

The visual inspiration for the game comes from a ‘PSX-style’ aesthetic, which features low-poly graphics and models to evoke the feeling of playing on older PlayStation models. According to the creator, this is popular among indie developers as an accessible way to bring ideas to life, while also leaving “more to the imagination”.

A trailer is expected to drop for the game in November, while the game itself is planned to release on Steam at the end of December. Hisham noted that success for him looks less like revenue and more like having an influence.

When asked, he said that players who are interested in narrative-driven indie titles and interactive worlds to explore are his target audience. Those who exclusively lean towards action-packed AAA titles will likely not get the fix they’re looking for — but those interested in a short, interactive and introspective story will want to keep an eye out for this at year end.

“Personally, for me, it doing well is just people talking about it … it having some sort of impact in the Pakistani indie game scene, because it’s pretty fragmented right now,” he told Dawn. “So people can be like, ‘Oh, this is something you can maybe do,’ and so there’s more people being really crazy about their art and just wanting to make something really good.”

He added, “I consider this a success if I finish this game exactly how I wanted to finish it, and if people care about it enough to talk about it and it leaves some sort of mark in the Pakistani indie scene. Even if not in a global way — as long as it has some sort of impact there, I’m happy.”

“I would say it’s more of a storyline that transcends,” he said. “It’s grounded in that culture and that setting, but the story itself revolves around a bunch of themes like dissociation, guilt — something that would be applicable to a wider audience.

Still, the game’s Pakistani roots and setting will be felt by players in another way: while the upcoming release of Fogbound will be in English, Hisham is planning to roll out a roman Urdu translation later so that it can reach the wider subcontinent. The art — featuring low-poly models deliberately designed to evoke old PlayStation games and a 3D-modelled city of Lahore — is all handled by one artist, while the music consists of 20-30 “dark ambient” tracks composed by a musician in Russia who was recruited to the project through Discord. The rest of it is entirely spearheaded and executed by Hisham.

The visual inspiration for the game comes from a ‘PSX-style’ aesthetic, which features low-poly graphics and models to evoke the feeling of playing on older PlayStation models. According to the creator, this is popular among indie developers as an accessible way to bring ideas to life, while also leaving “more to the imagination”.

A trailer is expected to drop for the game in November, while the game itself is planned to release on Steam at the end of December. Hisham noted that success for him looks less like revenue and more like having an influence.

When asked, he said that players who are interested in narrative-driven indie titles and interactive worlds to explore are his target audience. Those who exclusively lean towards action-packed AAA titles will likely not get the fix they’re looking for — but those interested in a short, interactive and introspective story will want to keep an eye out for this at year end.

“Personally, for me, it doing well is just people talking about it … it having some sort of impact in the Pakistani indie game scene, because it’s pretty fragmented right now,” he told Dawn. “So people can be like, ‘Oh, this is something you can maybe do,’ and so there’s more people being really crazy about their art and just wanting to make something really good.”

He added, “I consider this a success if I finish this game exactly how I wanted to finish it, and if people care about it enough to talk about it and it leaves some sort of mark in the Pakistani indie scene. Even if not in a global way — as long as it has some sort of impact there, I’m happy.”

headline: Israel blows up homes, shells towns in southern Lebanon
description: Israeli forces intensified attacks in southern Lebanon on Friday, blowing up homes and other structures while...
article_text:
Israeli forces intensified attacks in southern Lebanon on Friday, blowing up homes and other structures while carrying out artillery shelling and machine-gun fire in several areas, according to the Lebanese National News Agency (NNA).

Israeli forces carried out extensive machine-gun fire in the towns of Khiam and Qantara, while homes were also set on fire in Qantara, the NNA said.

The agency said the Israeli army carried out an explosion in the town of Tayri in the Bint Jbeil district, while artillery fire targeted Wadi al-Hujeir toward the town of Touline with 155-millimeter shells.

headline: 'Trump betrayed us': Arizona's Latino voters sour on president
description: National polls show widespread disillusionment among Latino voters, raising Democrats’ hopes of winning control of at least one house of Congress next week.
author: AFP
article_text:
Two years ago, Fernando Nunez went door-to-door in searing heat to help Donald Trump win Arizona and take back the White House.

But in next week’s midterm elections, he won’t be voting for candidates backed by the Republican president.

“Trump betrayed us. He did a whole 180,” said the 22-year-old American, whose family has Mexican roots.

Nunez had been drawn to the Republican billionaire’s promises: lowering prices, ending international wars, and releasing all of the files in the Jeffrey Epstein probe.

Now he is furious about the administration’s lack of transparency over Epstein — the late convicted sex offender who was a friend of Trump — as well as the war being waged against Iran, which has driven up gas prices and fueled broader inflation.

“Gas, insurance, food: everything went up and is more expensive than ever,” complained Nunez, who works as a sales rep and says he earns $1,600 a month.

“We’re not supposed to be at war with Iran. We’re only in this war because of Israel.”

Nunez says he will vote on November 3 for independent candidates — neither Republican nor Democratic.

Yuma County, where Nunez lives, perfectly illustrates the shift to the right within the Latino community in the United States, a trend that contributed to Trump’s victory in 2024.

In this corner of the Southwest, where the border wall between the United States and Mexico dominates the horizon, the Republican won by a 20-point margin.

‘Rude awakening’

In Somerton, an agricultural town whose population is almost entirely Latino and typically favours the Democrats, about 40 per cent of residents voted for Trump in 2024.

Mayor Gerardo Anaya says he thinks this was because they were angry at the runaway inflation seen under former president Joe Biden, as well as the daily influx of thousands of migrants.

“It was just a vote against the Biden administration,” the left-leaning mayor said.

But those who chose Trump are now experiencing a “rude awakening,” he added.

In this small town, which is surrounded by fields of lettuce, the parking lot of the only supermarket is abuzz with complaints.

Residents who spoke with AFP expressed outrage over the price of carne asada — a typical Mexican-style grilled meat — and the cost of diesel.

Rocketing gasoline prices have made a popular local pastime, driving off-road buggies in the desert, more expensive.

Trump’s image as a savvy businessman also no longer carries weight.

“I thought he was going to fix everything, but now I’m done. I don’t want anything to do with him anymore,” said one gardener, who preferred not to give his name.

‘Racist’

While the number of migrants at the border has dropped drastically, the gardener — who is of Mexican descent — said he could not accept the aggressive, large-scale enforcement raids taking place across the United States, some of which have led to the deportation of immigrants with no criminal records.

Trump “said he was going to go after criminals. That’s not what happened,” he says. “He’s a racist and that’s it.”

National polls show this sense of disillusionment among Latino voters is widespread, offering Democrats the hope that they can capitalise and seize control of at least one house of Congress next week.

But in Somerton, irritation with Trump does not necessarily translate into support for his opponents.

The gardener, for one, intends to abstain altogether.

At his hair salon, Jaime Sanchez remains undecided.

The 52-year-old had originally chosen Trump because of what he said was his opposition to abortion and his commitment to “family values.”

However, he admits to being troubled by the administration’s immigration policy, which can lead to the deportation of law-abiding adults, risking their separation from their American-born children.

“When a family isn’t united, there are greater dangers — more gangs, more drugs — because there’s no role model to provide guidance,” he said.

Jose Manuel Castro, an evangelical pastor from the neighbouring town of San Luis, told AFP he sees “a great deal of discontent.”

The 75-year-old conservative expects his congregation to cast a protest vote this time around.

In the long term, however, he believes that the shift of Latino voters, who tend to be religious, toward the Republican Party is only just beginning.

Many feel uncomfortable with an American Left that champions abortion and the rights of transgender individuals, he said.

“The Democratic Party promotes things that run counter to the principles of the Word of God,” he said.

“It was just a vote against the Biden administration,” the left-leaning mayor said.

But those who chose Trump are now experiencing a “rude awakening,” he added.

In this small town, which is surrounded by fields of lettuce, the parking lot of the only supermarket is abuzz with complaints.

Residents who spoke with AFP expressed outrage over the price of carne asada — a typical Mexican-style grilled meat — and the cost of diesel.

Rocketing gasoline prices have made a popular local pastime, driving off-road buggies in the desert, more expensive.

Trump’s image as a savvy businessman also no longer carries weight.

“I thought he was going to fix everything, but now I’m done. I don’t want anything to do with him anymore,” said one gardener, who preferred not to give his name.

While the number of migrants at the border has dropped drastically, the gardener — who is of Mexican descent — said he could not accept the aggressive, large-scale enforcement raids taking place across the United States, some of which have led to the deportation of immigrants with no criminal records.

Trump “said he was going to go after criminals. That’s not what happened,” he says. “He’s a racist and that’s it.”

National polls show this sense of disillusionment among Latino voters is widespread, offering Democrats the hope that they can capitalise and seize control of at least one house of Congress next week.

But in Somerton, irritation with Trump does not necessarily translate into support for his opponents.

The gardener, for one, intends to abstain altogether.

At his hair salon, Jaime Sanchez remains undecided.

The 52-year-old had originally chosen Trump because of what he said was his opposition to abortion and his commitment to “family values.”

However, he admits to being troubled by the administration’s immigration policy, which can lead to the deportation of law-abiding adults, risking their separation from their American-born children.

“When a family isn’t united, there are greater dangers — more gangs, more drugs — because there’s no role model to provide guidance,” he said.

Jose Manuel Castro, an evangelical pastor from the neighbouring town of San Luis, told AFP he sees “a great deal of discontent.”

The 75-year-old conservative expects his congregation to cast a protest vote this time around.

In the long term, however, he believes that the shift of Latino voters, who tend to be religious, toward the Republican Party is only just beginning.

Many feel uncomfortable with an American Left that champions abortion and the rights of transgender individuals, he said.

“The Democratic Party promotes things that run counter to the principles of the Word of God,” he said.

headline: Gen Z protests reach Germany as over 160,000 expected at Halloween rallies
description: The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs.
author: Reuters
article_text:
More than 160,000 people across Germany are expected to join demonstrations on Saturday, organisers say, as a youth-led movement inspired by protests elsewhere in Europe takes to the streets to demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests follow a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country’s long-time leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests, organised by campaign group Gen Z regelt (Gen Z takes charge), are planned in 34 cities including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs.

German authorities say they expect Saturday’s demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, to be largely peaceful but have warned of attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement.

Parts of Germany’s far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined efforts to mobilise support, according to the federal interior ministry.

“We all have those images from France in our minds - looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers,” said Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Germany’s financial hub, Frankfurt.

“France must not be held up as a model in this regard.” In Berlin, some businesses along the luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard boarded up windows and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations amid concerns about possible unrest.

Gen Z takes charge

For organisers, however, the focus is on what they see as the growing pressure on younger generations in Europe’s largest economy.

“The government has offered no response to our concerns other than to continue making cuts and piling further burdens upon us,” said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

“We will continue to exercise our fundamental right to assemble until you stop ignoring us.” The protests come as Germany struggles to revive economic growth while facing growing pressure on pensions and public services as baby boomers retire and the working-age population shrinks.

But questions have been raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany’s national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has distanced itself from the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on November 20.

“We are distancing ourselves from ‘Gen Z regelt,’ but not from the students themselves, who have legitimate concerns,” said BSK secretary-general Amy Kirchhoff on Thursday.

Sean Baker, a student at the Technical University of Berlin, said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention to the poor state of buildings on campus.

“When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building,” he told Reuters. “Yet this is where we’re expected to study on a regular basis.”

headline: Lebanon’s death toll from Israeli acts of aggression climbs to 8,956
description: Lebanon’s Health Ministry says 8,956 people have been killed and 30,664 wounded since October 2023, amid continued...
article_text:
Lebanon’s Health Ministry says 8,956 people have been killed and 30,664 wounded since October 2023, amid continued Israeli military aggression, IRNA reports.

The ministry reported that 4,389 people were killed and 12,428 injured between March 2 and October 30, 2026, Al-Manar TV network reported Friday night, citing the ministry.

The Israeli regime launched a large-scale offensive against Lebanon on March 2, displacing more than one million people. The regime’s forces continue to occupy areas in southern Lebanon.

“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region,” Turki al-Malki said, adding that “debris from the interception fell without causing injuries”.

headline: US, South Korea, Japan vow 'complete' North Korea denuclearisation
description: Countries pledge “full implementation” of UNSC resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea's nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.
author: AFP
article_text:
The United States, South Korea and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the “complete denuclearisation” of North Korea on Saturday, as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible talks with Washington.

Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearisation” of North Korea during talks on Friday on the sidelines of a Group of 20 (G20) meeting in Atlanta in the US state of Georgia, the US State Department said.

They also pledged “full implementation” of UN Security Council resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea, which is backed by Russia and China, has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.

Open to meeting

Trump has made repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks, while scaling back joint military drills with ally South Korea.

The mercurial US leader even bucked long-held US policy last year by conceding that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”, while reaching out to Pyongyang for talks, saying he was “100 per cent” open to a meeting — a suggestion that went unanswered.

Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency say Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on potential talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong.

South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung — who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief.

Critics have said such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal.

Analysts say China may also be moving towards tacit acceptance, pointing to the omission of North Korean denuclearisation from statements after Kim and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in June.

Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks.

They also pledged “full implementation” of UN Security Council resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea, which is backed by Russia and China, has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.

Open to meeting

Trump has made repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks, while scaling back joint military drills with ally South Korea.

The mercurial US leader even bucked long-held US policy last year by conceding that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”, while reaching out to Pyongyang for talks, saying he was “100 per cent” open to a meeting — a suggestion that went unanswered.

Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency say Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on potential talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong.

South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung — who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief.

Critics have said such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal.

Analysts say China may also be moving towards tacit acceptance, pointing to the omission of North Korean denuclearisation from statements after Kim and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in June.

Pyongyang denounced a joint statement on Saturday by a group of nations monitoring sanctions implementation against it, vowing that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”.

headline: Three-year-old child tests positive for mpox in Sindh
description: Sources said the three-year-old boy was currently under treatment at Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre.
author: Faiza Ilyas
article_text:
KARACHI: Another child tested positive for mpox in the city on Friday, raising the tally of the viral infectious disease this year so far in the province to 115.

Mpox is a viral infection which was earlier restricted to international travellers. It spreads through close contact with someone who has mpox, contaminated bedding, towels, medical instruments, surfaces or objects.

Sources said the three-year-old boy was currently under treatment at Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre (SIDH&RC).

“Like the recent two cases, this child also underwent circumcision at the same Malir hospital that has been officially sealed over concerns related to lack of infection control measures,” a hospital doctor said, adding that an infant with mpox died early this week after remaining under treatment for 10 days at the facility while another was in the intensive care.

He also shared that the seven mpox patients currently under treatment at SIDH&RC included the mother and an aunt of the infant who died fighting mpox — the first infant’s death in Karachi this year.

With the latest case, the total number of mpox cases reported this year so far at SIDH&RC has risen to 31, while in the province to 115 with 12 deaths.

The Sindh Health Care Commission (SHCC) had sealed Ibne Hassan Hospital over 10 days ago following a laboratory report confirming an mpox case in an infant, after concerns were identified regarding infection prevention and control practices.

“The hospital was legal but not registered with the SHCC. The team sealed the facility following reports that a child seemed to have contracted mpox there. The team during inspection found a dispenser conducting circumcision, a procedure that was beyond his scope,” explained Dr Ahson Qavi Siddiqi, the chief executive officer of SHCC.

The hospital, he said, was opened on Friday for sanitisation, fumigation and disinfection, and sealed again. “This exercise will continue for some time and then sampling [to see if the facility is safe and fit for operation] will be carried out. The concerned party is also required to submit certain legal documents, too. All this will lead to a decision on the case.”

Published in Dawn, October 31st, 2026

headline: Mayor Murtaza Wahab opens Method and Madness
description: The festival has brought together around 1,000 international artists from more than 150 countries, alongside 500 Pakistani artists, transforming Karachi into a vibrant meeting point of world cultures.
author: Peerzada Salman
article_text:
KARACHI: Method and Madness, the first exhibition out of five planned during the World Culture Festival, was opened by Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab on Friday.

After witnessing the artworks on view made by 12 international and 14 Pakistani artists, Mr Wahab spoke to the media and the artists at the Arts Council, Karachi.

He welcomed them all to Karachi and hoped they would enjoy their stay in the city and their interaction with fellow artists.

During the exhibition, speaking to Dawn, Ireland’s ambassador to Pakistan Mary O’Neill said the atmosphere at the event was super exciting. “It’s great to see artists from around the world.”

Answering a question about the importance of holding such events at a time when the world is faced with conflicts, she said these events are important because they transcend circumstances.

The festival has brought together around 1,000 international artists from more than 150 countries, alongside 500 Pakistani artists, transforming Karachi into a vibrant meeting point of world cultures.

The 25-day festival, scheduled to be ended on Nov 22, offers an extraordinary platform for artists, performers, writers and creative communities from across the globe to share their cultural traditions, social norms, culinary practices, literary expressions and contemporary artistic trends.

The World Culture Festival - Karachi 2026 features an extensive programme of music, theatre, dance, visual arts, films, workshops, live mural painting, fine arts sessions and interactive cultural discussions.

Pakistani folk traditions, qawwali, contemporary music and theatrical productions are being presented alongside international performances, creating opportunities for artistic learning, collaboration and cross-cultural engagement.

With artists and cultural representatives from more than 150 countries, the festival offers a remarkable opportunity to experience the diversity of human civilisation under one roof.

headline: Three held for injuring scooty-riding female in Kasur
description: Police claimed to have traced the whereabouts of the suspects with the help of safe city cameras and arrested them.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
KASUR: The A-Division police arrested three suspects on Friday for injuring a female college student by pushing her scooty at Baldia Chowk near the Government Girls College.

As per details, the suspects had allegedly chased the student ‘N’ and harassed her while she was on her way home on her scooty on Thursday.

Later, they pushed her moving vehicle near the Baldia Chowk, as a result, she fell and suffered injuries.

She was later hospitalised and the video of the injured student also made rounds on social media.

Police claimed to have traced the whereabouts of the suspects with the help of safe city cameras and arrested them. Police said legal proceedings and investigations were ongoing.

KABADDI: Sports inculcate discipline and a spirit of teamwork among youth and help them attain a healthy lifestyle, said Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmed Khan after a kabaddi match held at Khudian Khas in connection with Khelta Punjab on Friday.

He said the provincial government had initiated sports programmes to provide youth with a platform to showcase their talent and develop a healthy lifestyle instead of spending most of their time on mobile screens. Healthy activities would also keep youth away from narcotics, he added.

Appreciating the sports programmes of the chief minister, he said that it was reviving the culture that promoted talent from the grassroot level and helped them compete at the international level.

headline: Yemeni army claims 336 Houthis neutralised in 'Dawn of Yemen' operation
description: Yemen’s armed forces said they had neutralized around 336 Houthi fighters and commanders during ongoing military...
article_text:
Yemen’s armed forces said they had neutralised around 336 Houthi fighters and commanders during ongoing military operations under the “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, Anadolu reports.

Military spokesman Col. Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili said government forces had carried out 1,087 strikes in recent hours using warplanes, drones, field artillery, and rocket launchers.

He said the strikes targeted Houthi command and control centers, troop concentrations, reinforcements, firing positions, fortifications, and supply routes.

Muslim Americans take on key electoral contests in midterms amid foreign policy debates
description: From congressional races to local government, Muslim Americans are seeking greater representation as the wars in Gaza and Iran intensify debate over US foreign policy.
author: Anwar Iqbal
article_text:
WASHINGTON: Muslim Americans are seeking a greater voice in US politics in the November 3 midterm elections, with candidates contesting congressional, state legislative and local offices across the country.

Their campaigns come amid growing controversy over Washington’s Middle East policy. The war in Gaza has fuelled demands for an end to US military support for Israel, while the war with Iran has raised questions about American intervention, regional stability and overseas military spending.

Muslim Network TV (MNTV), reviewing candidate listings and cross-checking names against civic organisations’ voter guides, officeholder records and news reports, has identified at least 51 Muslim Americans running across approximately 23 states. The count includes one Senate candidate, 10 congressional candidates and dozens seeking state and local offices. It represents a documented minimum, not a comprehensive national census.

One of the most closely watched contests is Michigan’s Senate race, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is seeking to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

Virginia Lieutenant Governor Ghazala Hashmi, the first Muslim woman elected to statewide office in the United States, endorsed El-Sayed in September, citing their shared commitment to affordable housing, healthcare, workers’ rights and economic opportunity.

El-Sayed’s campaign has also attracted attacks centred on his faith. At a Michigan rally on October 25, President Donald Trump called him a “jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member” and suggested he should not be allowed into the Senate. El-Sayed has denied any association with the organisation, and reporting has found no evidence that he belongs to it.

Addressing the broader question of Muslim American identity, El-Sayed said: “They want to tell us that this country is not ours. They want to tell us that because of our names and how we pray, somehow we are less than them.”

Minnesota Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, a Democrat seeking re-election, has faced similar attacks from Trump, who has questioned her patriotism and revived allegations about her immigration history. Omar has rejected the administration’s actions as political intimidation, saying: “I will not be silenced.”

The war in Gaza has become another major issue in the campaigns. Many Muslim and Arab American voters are demanding that Washington reconsider its military support for Israel, although opposition to continued assistance also extends to progressive activists, younger Democrats and some Jewish Americans.

El-Sayed has called Israel’s conduct in Gaza genocide and demanded an end to US military assistance. He has also opposed funding foreign militaries generally, including those of Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

In an interview with Democracy Now! after winning the Democratic primary in August, he linked overseas military spending to economic pressures at home.

“In an era where many of us can’t afford basic things like groceries or rent or healthcare, the idea that your government is sending your tax dollars to buy bombs and tanks for foreign governments seems anathema,” he said. “That money could be spent to fix your potholes, rebuild your kid’s school, that looks like it did 50 years ago. And we need that money spent here.”

Michigan Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, also seeking re-election, has demanded a full arms embargo against Israel. On July 2, she renewed her call, arguing that American military support enabled abuses against Palestinians.

The positions of El-Sayed and Tlaib contrast with those of lawmakers who consider military assistance essential to Israel’s security and American strategic interests. The debate has become particularly contentious as criticism of Israeli policy is sometimes portrayed as evidence of hostility towards Israel or questionable loyalty to the United States.

The Iran war has added urgency to these foreign-policy debates. US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, 2026, triggering Iranian retaliation and a wider regional conflict. Diplomatic and ceasefire efforts have failed to produce a durable settlement.

On October 28, The Associated Press reported that US officials had warned Middle Eastern countries and regional allies to prepare for possible renewed American strikes on Iran after the midterm elections, as well as potential Iranian retaliation. Trump had not made a final decision but had repeatedly indicated that further military action remained an option.

The prospect of renewed fighting has raised concerns about energy supplies, fuel prices and the financial costs of a prolonged conflict. These issues could resonate well beyond Muslim communities, particularly as voters weigh overseas military commitments against domestic economic pressures.

The 51 candidates identified by MNTV represent a broader political presence extending beyond prominent national figures. They are contesting offices that influence education, healthcare, housing, employment, public safety and civil rights, as well as national legislation and foreign policy.

Civic organisations are also working to register Muslim voters and encourage turnout. A survey released by the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and CAIR Action on October 28 examined Muslim voters’ intentions and priorities, including economic pressures, Gaza and concerns about anti-Muslim hostility.

Muslim Americans, however, do not vote as a single bloc. Their political affiliations and positions on domestic and international issues vary, and their candidacies reflect a range of political priorities rather than a unified religious platform.

The midterm results will determine control of the House of Representatives and influence the balance of power in the Senate, with consequences for congressional oversight, military funding and the administration’s freedom of action.

El-Sayed’s Senate contest will attract particular attention, but the significance of Muslim American participation extends well beyond one race. Their growing presence in electoral politics reflects a determination to influence decisions affecting their communities and the country’s role in the world.

The broader test is whether American voters will judge these candidates by their policies and records rather than treating their religious identity as a measure of their patriotism.

article_html:
WASHINGTON: Muslim Americans are seeking a greater voice in US politics in the November 3 midterm elections, with candidates contesting congressional, state legislative and local offices across the country.

Their campaigns come amid growing controversy over Washington’s Middle East policy. The war in Gaza has fuelled demands for an end to US military support for Israel, while the war with Iran has raised questions about American intervention, regional stability and overseas military spending.

Muslim Network TV (MNTV), reviewing candidate listings and cross-checking names against civic organisations’ voter guides, officeholder records and news reports, has identified at least 51 Muslim Americans running across approximately 23 states. The count includes one Senate candidate, 10 congressional candidates and dozens seeking state and local offices. It represents a documented minimum, not a comprehensive national census.

One of the most closely watched contests is Michigan’s Senate race, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is seeking to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

Virginia Lieutenant Governor Ghazala Hashmi, the first Muslim woman elected to statewide office in the United States, endorsed El-Sayed in September, citing their shared commitment to affordable housing, healthcare, workers’ rights and economic opportunity.

El-Sayed’s campaign has also attracted attacks centred on his faith. At a Michigan rally on October 25, President Donald Trump called him a “jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member” and suggested he should not be allowed into the Senate. El-Sayed has denied any association with the organisation, and reporting has found no evidence that he belongs to it.

Addressing the broader question of Muslim American identity, El-Sayed said: “They want to tell us that this country is not ours. They want to tell us that because of our names and how we pray, somehow we are less than them.”

Minnesota Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, a Democrat seeking re-election, has faced similar attacks from Trump, who has questioned her patriotism and revived allegations about her immigration history. Omar has rejected the administration’s actions as political intimidation, saying: “I will not be silenced.”

The war in Gaza has become another major issue in the campaigns. Many Muslim and Arab American voters are demanding that Washington reconsider its military support for Israel, although opposition to continued assistance also extends to progressive activists, younger Democrats and some Jewish Americans.

El-Sayed has called Israel’s conduct in Gaza genocide and demanded an end to US military assistance. He has also opposed funding foreign militaries generally, including those of Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

In an interview with Democracy Now! after winning the Democratic primary in August, he linked overseas military spending to economic pressures at home.

“In an era where many of us can’t afford basic things like groceries or rent or healthcare, the idea that your government is sending your tax dollars to buy bombs and tanks for foreign governments seems anathema,” he said. “That money could be spent to fix your potholes, rebuild your kid’s school, that looks like it did 50 years ago. And we need that money spent here.”

Michigan Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, also seeking re-election, has demanded a full arms embargo against Israel. On July 2, she renewed her call, arguing that American military support enabled abuses against Palestinians.

The positions of El-Sayed and Tlaib contrast with those of lawmakers who consider military assistance essential to Israel’s security and American strategic interests. The debate has become particularly contentious as criticism of Israeli policy is sometimes portrayed as evidence of hostility towards Israel or questionable loyalty to the United States.

The Iran war has added urgency to these foreign-policy debates. US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, 2026, triggering Iranian retaliation and a wider regional conflict. Diplomatic and ceasefire efforts have failed to produce a durable settlement.

On October 28, The Associated Press reported that US officials had warned Middle Eastern countries and regional allies to prepare for possible renewed American strikes on Iran after the midterm elections, as well as potential Iranian retaliation. Trump had not made a final decision but had repeatedly indicated that further military action remained an option.

The prospect of renewed fighting has raised concerns about energy supplies, fuel prices and the financial costs of a prolonged conflict. These issues could resonate well beyond Muslim communities, particularly as voters weigh overseas military commitments against domestic economic pressures.

The 51 candidates identified by MNTV represent a broader political presence extending beyond prominent national figures. They are contesting offices that influence education, healthcare, housing, employment, public safety and civil rights, as well as national legislation and foreign policy.

Civic organisations are also working to register Muslim voters and encourage turnout. A survey released by the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and CAIR Action on October 28 examined Muslim voters’ intentions and priorities, including economic pressures, Gaza and concerns about anti-Muslim hostility.

Muslim Americans, however, do not vote as a single bloc. Their political affiliations and positions on domestic and international issues vary, and their candidacies reflect a range of political priorities rather than a unified religious platform.

The midterm results will determine control of the House of Representatives and influence the balance of power in the Senate, with consequences for congressional oversight, military funding and the administration’s freedom of action.

El-Sayed’s Senate contest will attract particular attention, but the significance of Muslim American participation extends well beyond one race. Their growing presence in electoral politics reflects a determination to influence decisions affecting their communities and the country’s role in the world.

The broader test is whether American voters will judge these candidates by their policies and records rather than treating their religious identity as a measure of their patriotism.

WASHINGTON: Muslim Americans are seeking a greater voice in US politics in the November 3 midterm elections, with candidates contesting congressional, state legislative and local offices across the country.

Their campaigns come amid growing controversy over Washington’s Middle East policy. The war in Gaza has fuelled demands for an end to US military support for Israel, while the war with Iran has raised questions about American intervention, regional stability and overseas military spending.

Muslim Network TV (MNTV), reviewing candidate listings and cross-checking names against civic organisations’ voter guides, officeholder records and news reports, has identified at least 51 Muslim Americans running across approximately 23 states. The count includes one Senate candidate, 10 congressional candidates and dozens seeking state and local offices. It represents a documented minimum, not a comprehensive national census.

One of the most closely watched contests is Michigan’s Senate race, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is seeking to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

Virginia Lieutenant Governor Ghazala Hashmi, the first Muslim woman elected to statewide office in the United States, endorsed El-Sayed in September, citing their shared commitment to affordable housing, healthcare, workers’ rights and economic opportunity.

El-Sayed’s campaign has also attracted attacks centred on his faith. At a Michigan rally on October 25, President Donald Trump called him a “jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member” and suggested he should not be allowed into the Senate. El-Sayed has denied any association with the organisation, and reporting has found no evidence that he belongs to it.

Addressing the broader question of Muslim American identity, El-Sayed said: “They want to tell us that this country is not ours. They want to tell us that because of our names and how we pray, somehow we are less than them.”

Minnesota Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, a Democrat seeking re-election, has faced similar attacks from Trump, who has questioned her patriotism and revived allegations about her immigration history. Omar has rejected the administration’s actions as political intimidation, saying: “I will not be silenced.”

The war in Gaza has become another major issue in the campaigns. Many Muslim and Arab American voters are demanding that Washington reconsider its military support for Israel, although opposition to continued assistance also extends to progressive activists, younger Democrats and some Jewish Americans.

El-Sayed has called Israel’s conduct in Gaza genocide and demanded an end to US military assistance. He has also opposed funding foreign militaries generally, including those of Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

In an interview with Democracy Now! after winning the Democratic primary in August, he linked overseas military spending to economic pressures at home.

“In an era where many of us can’t afford basic things like groceries or rent or healthcare, the idea that your government is sending your tax dollars to buy bombs and tanks for foreign governments seems anathema,” he said. “That money could be spent to fix your potholes, rebuild your kid’s school, that looks like it did 50 years ago. And we need that money spent here.”

Michigan Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, also seeking re-election, has demanded a full arms embargo against Israel. On July 2, she renewed her call, arguing that American military support enabled abuses against Palestinians.

The positions of El-Sayed and Tlaib contrast with those of lawmakers who consider military assistance essential to Israel’s security and American strategic interests. The debate has become particularly contentious as criticism of Israeli policy is sometimes portrayed as evidence of hostility towards Israel or questionable loyalty to the United States.

The Iran war has added urgency to these foreign-policy debates. US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, 2026, triggering Iranian retaliation and a wider regional conflict. Diplomatic and ceasefire efforts have failed to produce a durable settlement.

On October 28, The Associated Press reported that US officials had warned Middle Eastern countries and regional allies to prepare for possible renewed American strikes on Iran after the midterm elections, as well as potential Iranian retaliation. Trump had not made a final decision but had repeatedly indicated that further military action remained an option.

The prospect of renewed fighting has raised concerns about energy supplies, fuel prices and the financial costs of a prolonged conflict. These issues could resonate well beyond Muslim communities, particularly as voters weigh overseas military commitments against domestic economic pressures.

The 51 candidates identified by MNTV represent a broader political presence extending beyond prominent national figures. They are contesting offices that influence education, healthcare, housing, employment, public safety and civil rights, as well as national legislation and foreign policy.

Civic organisations are also working to register Muslim voters and encourage turnout. A survey released by the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and CAIR Action on October 28 examined Muslim voters’ intentions and priorities, including economic pressures, Gaza and concerns about anti-Muslim hostility.

Muslim Americans, however, do not vote as a single bloc. Their political affiliations and positions on domestic and international issues vary, and their candidacies reflect a range of political priorities rather than a unified religious platform.

The midterm results will determine control of the House of Representatives and influence the balance of power in the Senate, with consequences for congressional oversight, military funding and the administration’s freedom of action.

El-Sayed’s Senate contest will attract particular attention, but the significance of Muslim American participation extends well beyond one race. Their growing presence in electoral politics reflects a determination to influence decisions affecting their communities and the country’s role in the world.

The broader test is whether American voters will judge these candidates by their policies and records rather than treating their religious identity as a measure of their patriotism.

headline: US oil companies aim to squeeze more out of refineries
description: US oil companies are investing to squeeze out more fuel from refineries and bringing shuttered plants back online in...
article_text:
US oil companies are investing to squeeze out more fuel from refineries and bringing shuttered plants back online in response to conflicts in Russia and Iran that have crimped supplies, Reuters reports.

ExxonMobil Chief Executive Darren Woods said Friday the company had achieved “record fuels utilization” outside of the Middle East, pointing to 100 percent crude utilization at US Gulf Coast refineries.

The statements come as US gasoline prices remain above the politically sensitive $4 per gallon level and as diesel prices linger near all-time highs above $6 per gallon.

“In the third quarter, we continued to rise to the challenge of meeting global energy needs,” Woods said in a press release.

article_text:
Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said he was “extremely worried” that a new round of escalation in the war between the United States and Iran would be more destructive and have a major impact, Reuters reports.

headline: Singapore FM’s visit focused on enhancing cooperation in trade, infrastructure and digital technologies: FO
description: Two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral ties and exchanged views on regional and international developments, FO says.
author: News Desk
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and his Singaporean counterpart Dr Vivian Balakrishnan discussed ways to enhance bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, agriculture, infrastructure development and digital technologies during the latter’s visit to Pakistan, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.

At the invitation of Dar, Dr Balakrishnan undertook an official visit to Pakistan on Friday.

According to a statement issued by the FO today, the two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral ties and exchanged views on regional and international developments.

“Deepening of Pakistan’s engagement with Asean, including in the context of Singapore’s upcoming Asean chairmanship in 2027, also came under discussion,” the statement added.

The two ministers also exchanged a memorandum of understanding on cooperation in disaster management between Pakistan’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Singapore’s Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

The MoU aims to strengthen cooperation in disaster preparedness, response and resilience, the FO said.

Coinciding with the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, the visit reflected their shared commitment to further strengthening their longstanding partnership, it added.

On Friday, Dr Balakrishnan met Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters, where the two discussed regional security and avenues for bilateral cooperation.

He also called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who expressed admiration for Singapore’s “remarkable economic transformation” and its achievements in innovation and development.

The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral fora.

Separately, Dar discussed with the visiting diplomat the possible resumption of direct flights between Pakistan and Singapore to facilitate business travel and closer contact between the two peoples.

headline: Court grants bail to anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan, lawyer confirms
description: NCCIA tells the court that no further investigation involving Hassan is required.
author: Sumair Abdullah
article_text:
KARACHI: A judicial magistrate granted bail to anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan, his lawyer, Advocate Ahmad Masood, confirmed to Dawn on Saturday.

The anchorperson was arrested by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in a case registered in Karachi for allegedly disseminating anti-state, false and defamatory content through his official social media accounts. He was booked under multiple sections of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

Hassan, who was in judicial custody, was granted bail on Saturday against surety bonds of Rs200,000 by East Judicial Magistrate Gulraiz Memon, Advocate Masood said.

“The challan has been submitted to the court, and his electronic devices have been taken into possession by the authorities,” he said.

Meanwhile, during the hearing, the NCCIA told the court that no further investigation involving Hassan was required, but it was awaiting a forensic report.

On October 22, the same judicial magistrate rejected a bail plea filed by Hassan, prompting the defence to challenge the rejection in a sessions court.

During the October 22 hearing, the NCCIA submitted its remand report, saying the investigation had progressed but several important aspects remained to be examined in light of the forensic analysis of Hassan’s seized digital devices and records from other departments, including the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra).

In a verdict issued by the local court, the court held that it did not find any merit in the bail application and dismissed the same accordingly.

“However, the counsel for the applicant/accused may move a bail application before the trial court, as the challan/charge sheet has been submitted before the learned trial court subsequent to the dismissal of the applicant’s earlier bail application by the said court, said the Sessions Court, providing the grounds for the trial court to approve the bail following the submission of the challan.

On October 19, the judicial magistrate sent the anchorperson to prison on an eight-day judicial remand until October 26.

On October 17, Hassan was produced before Judicial Magistrate Memon upon the completion of his initial four-day physical remand. The NCCIA had sought a further 10 days of custody for questioning, but the magistrate rejected the request and granted the agency two more days.

headline: Prime suspect in Gujranwala bride's murder killed in alleged exchange of fire, claims CCD
description: CCD spokesperson claims that the suspects had been constantly changing locations before their arrest the previous night.
author: Imran Gabol
article_text:
LAHORE: The Crime Control Department (CCD) claimed on Saturday that the prime suspect in the murder of a bride on her wedding day in Gujranwala district was killed during an alleged exchange of fire.

According to a CCD spokesperson, the prime suspect, Sarfraz, had allegedly been hiding in Karachi with the other suspects before being arrested.

The spokesperson claimed that while he was being transported back by the CCD, the convoy came under attack. Sarfraz was allegedly killed by gunfire from his own accomplices during the exchange of fire.

The spokesperson further claimed that the suspects, including a woman, had been constantly changing locations before their arrest the previous night.

The bride was shot dead on the day of her reception in Gujranwala city, allegedly by the prime suspect whose marriage proposal was declined by her family.

According to the CCD Gujranwala, the suspect opened fire on her after stopping her vehicle as she returned from her wedding reception.

A department spokesperson said the case was registered at a CCD police station on the complaint of the deceased’s father. The Gujranwala CCD booked three suspects — Sarfraz, his female cousin and an unidentified accomplice — under sections 302 (premeditated murder), 311 (Ta’zir after waiver or compounding of right of qisas in qatl-i-amd), 109 (punishment for abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment) and 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The CCD, established last year, has been criticised by human rights advocates and civil society members for a high number of casualties.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) alleged earlier this year that the CCD has adopted a “deliberate policy of staged police encounters leading to extrajudicial killings”. In response, the department termed the claims as unfounded and contrary to the department’s operational framework.

A day earlier, the CCD claimed that two alleged robbers were “killed during an encounter” in Punjab’s Kasur. Police claimed the suspects were wanted by Kasur, Lahore and Sheikhupura police in dozens of cases of robbery, house dacoities and murders.

On October 29, the department claimed that a man involved in a case of a murder of a 10-year-old boy was also allegedly killed in an encounter.

Earlier this week, the CCD released a comparison of crime figures of September 2023-24 and September 2025-26, claiming 63 per cent reduction in overall crime, including robbery and motorcycle theft, across Punjab.

According to the CCD spokesperson, Lahore recorded the steepest decline in overall crime, at 78pc, in September 2025-26 compared to September 2023-24. Faisalabad followed with a 68pc decrease and Sahiwal with 66pc. Multan recorded a 59pc decline, while Gujranwala and Bahawalpur each saw a 58pc decrease. Crime rates also fell by 57pc in Sheikhupura, 56pc in Sargodha, 52pc in Rawalpindi and 43pc in Dera Ghazi Khan.

headline: Shooting at California Halloween store kills one, wounds six
description: At least three of those shot are in critical condition, local police chief says.
author: AFP
article_text:
A shooting at a Halloween store in northern California killed one person and wounded six on Friday, police said, adding investigators had not yet identified who was responsible.

The incident occurred shortly before 8:30pm (0330 GMT Saturday) at a Spirit Halloween store at a shopping mall in Fairfield, about 47 miles (76 kilometres) northeast of San Francisco.

Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall told reporters one person was killed and six others were hospitalised with gunshot wounds. At least three were in critical condition, he added.

“There is still a very active crime scene and investigation going on right now,” Marshall said late Friday, noting police had not yet identified the “suspect or suspects” responsible.

The shooting took place hours before the start of Halloween, which is celebrated in the United States on Saturday.

Marshall said no areas outside of the Solano Town Centre mall were on lockdown.

On October 26, a shooting near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee left 11 people with gunshot wounds and another injured, authorities said.

The shooting took place near Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University’s campus on Perry Street, the university said, while police counted six adults and six juveniles among the injured.

headline: Iranian supreme leader orders military response without 'geographic limits' to new threats

Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, in strategic directives to senior armed forces commanders, says that “every form of enemy threat must be met with immediate response, without geographical limitations,” Press TV reports.

“All material and non-material assets of the US-Israeli enemy must be within Iran’s reach,” the supreme leader said.

“If the enemies once again begin military or terrorist attacks, it is the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions of its end.

“Intelligent combat readiness for a powerful confrontation with enemies is a fundamental prerequisite for achieving maximum deterrence.”

Armed forces, nation would determine timing and terms of any future war, Mojtaba said.

headline: Two fishermen missing after attack in Hormuz: Iranian official
description: Two fishermen are missing and two others injured in an attack on two boats in the Strait of Hormuz, AFP reports...
article_text:
Two fishermen are missing and two others injured in an attack on two boats in the Strait of Hormuz, AFP reports citing an official who blames the United States for the incident.

“An attack by the American enemy occurred around 11:30am (1pm PKT) today on two fishing boats, each carrying two people, near Qeshm Island,” says Ahmad Nafisi, Deputy Provincial Governor of Hormozgan, according to state TV.

“Two of those were transported to Qeshm and the other two remain missing while search and rescue operations are currently underway to locate them,” he adds.
