headline: Power bills and data centres cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms
description: Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services, and bills in battleground states like Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania have grown even faster.
author: Reuters
article_text:
US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year’s midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centres.

Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10 per cent since 2024, when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in both houses of the US Congress.

Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services. Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centres. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.

Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps that could have sweeping consequences for the country’s utility industry.

“It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms,” said Charles Hua, executive director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favour consumers. “Part of that is because people’s utility bills have gone up and up, and they don’t see any end in sight.”

Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities’ requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity utilities can earn on their grid investments.

This year, utilities are on track to match last year’s record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed. Last year’s spending was double the previous record.

The investor-owned companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Globals Regulatory Research Associates.

Utilities spotlighted

Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia.

Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not directly elected.

In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was “not beholden to utility companies” and work with the state attorney general to crack down on “excessive rate hikes and predatory practices.”

Ohio’s residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20pc over the last two years, according to EIA data.

Acton has also said she supports a data centre moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centres would not pay electricity bills at all.

Bully pulpit

Some governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down.

In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that the prominent PECO Energy Company had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month.

He followed up with a letter to more utility chief executives seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns on equity.

“The governors are using this crisis on energy affordability as an opportunity to take a deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense,” said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Centre for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.

Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills. She did so the same day she took office.

In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centres in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year’s elections.

Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid.

“The grid is America’s greatest machine, and it doesn’t operate on the political calendar, said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organisation for investor-owned electric utilities. “It requires consistent investment every year to deliver reliable energy to our customers.”

Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to “deteriorating” from “neutral” in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits.

For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households.

“I do think the real meat will come after the election,” Hua said.

headline: China green channel
description: The green channel is a useful step, given Pakistan identifies which agricultural products it can export, meets Chinese quality standards, and builds dependable supply chains.
author: Editorial
article_text:
THE agreement between Islamabad and Beijing to set up a green channel at the Sost-Khunjerab border for agricultural and allied products should ease bilateral cross-border trade.

Priority customs processing, risk-based inspections and faster clearance of perishables should cut delays and the cost of moving goods. The question is if it will help Pakistan’s agricultural exports.

The two customs administrations will share information, including risk alerts, which should speed up inspections without loosening oversight. Quick clearance matters most for farm produce, which spoils if held up, costing growers money and competitiveness. Reliable access to the Chinese market could help farmers and exporters find new buyers and earn more foreign exchange.

The trade gap shows how much remains to be done. Last year, Pakistan Customs collected a record Rs15bn in revenue on imports through Khunjerab, while exports to China and Central Asia via the route came to just Rs2.8bn. The two figures measure different things and cannot be compared directly. But they do show how little we export through this corridor.

Pakistan needs to identify which agricultural products it can export, meet Chinese quality standards, and build dependable supply chains. Fruit and vegetables from Gilgit-Baltistan and other northern areas stand to gain from better access. However, exporters need cold storage, refrigerated transport, grading and packaging facilities, and predictable logistics.

Weather is another constraint. The Khunjerab Pass is generally open for trade and travel from April to November; heavy snow shuts it in winter. Both countries should work towards keeping it open year-round. A green channel is of little use if exporters cannot count on the route for regular deliveries throughout the year.

The initiative can also be seen in the wider context of CPEC. Pakistan has tended to treat its economic relationship with Beijing mainly as a source of infrastructure investment and imports. Market access, local business participation and two-way trade deserve equal weight.

There is no doubt that exchanging customs documents electronically should remove procedural bottlenecks and also curb under-invoicing of Chinese imports, which remains a serious drain on the exchequer.

Beijing’s reported exports exceed Pakistan’s recorded imports from China by around $5bn, a gap that points to large-scale misdeclaration at the border and heavy revenue losses. It is time this too was fixed. Honest valuation would shield local producers and manufacturers from unfair competition and factory closures.

The green channel is a useful step, but it should be judged by results: growth in Pakistani exports, the number of businesses reaching the Chinese market, and the income of domestic producers.

Published in Dawn, October 31st, 2026

headline: Iran's army warns any new US attack would spread war wider
description: Iran’s army warned Saturday that any new US attack would only spread their war wider, following threats by America...
article_text:
Iran’s army has warned that any new US attack would only spread their war wider, following threats by America and Israel of further military action as they hold crucial elections, AFP reports.

The Iranian warning comes with fresh diplomatic efforts underway to avert a resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators in Tehran and US Vice President JD Vance reportedly sending a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

“If the US president once again embarks on more regional adventurism under pressure from, and in an attempt to appease, the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said without elaborating.

headline: ‘Very little, if anything, done for KP’: PM Shehbaz rails against PTI’s governance in province
description: Premier says federal government was compelled to impose an emergency and governor’s rule in the province as it had no other option.
author: News Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday criticised PTI’s governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, questioning whether the funds available to the now dysfunctional provincial government had been used transparently for the welfare and betterment of the people of the province.

His remarks came during a meeting of the PML-N’s parliamentary party from KP, held in Islamabad.

The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move had drawn criticism from the opposition, as well as Fazl, who had made efforts to reduce tensions between the federal and the KP governments.

Taking aim at the PTI, Prime Minister Shehbaz said: “They have been in power in KP for 13 years. Over these 13 years, they have raised countless slogans, delivered fiery speeches, held long marches and sit-ins, and made numerous promises.”

Recalling PTI’s promises to build hundreds of dams, generate hundreds of megawatts of solar power, and establish hospitals, universities and schools across the province, the prime minister questioned whether any of these pledges had been fulfilled during the party’s 13 years in power.

“How many universities have been established there? How many new hospitals have been built? How much has the healthcare system improved? What facilities have actually been provided to the people? And how much corruption has taken place in the process?” he asked.

The prime minister also questioned whether public funds had been utilised transparently for the welfare and betterment of the people of KP.

“From Peshawar to Kohistan and Hazara, and across the entire southern region of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the majority of people would tell you that the PTI government has done very little, if anything, to address their basic needs,” he said.

The premier maintained that by 2017-18, terrorist activities in the province had been brought to an end to “a considerable extent”.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was among the provinces that made the greatest sacrifices in the fight against terrorism,” he said.

The prime minister highlighted the heavy toll terrorism had taken on the country, saying around 80,000 people had lost their lives and Pakistan’s economy had suffered losses estimated at Rs15,000 billion.

He also praised former prime minister and PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif for his policies to combat terrorism following the 2014 Army Public School tragedy, in which more than 140 students and teachers were killed.

Turning to the PTI, the prime minister said the party had spent the past two and a half years engaged in long marches and protests.

“In 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping was scheduled to visit Pakistan. We made repeated efforts to persuade the party to call off its sit-in so that President Xi’s visit could proceed as planned, but it refused. As a result, the visit was postponed,” he said, recalling the 2014 D-Chowk protest.

He also criticised the PTI for allowing “brutal terrorists” from Afghanistan to settle in Swat.

“These were among the most painful and heartrending incidents that allowed terrorism to regain momentum,” he said.

The premier further said that thousands of civilians and security personnel had been martyred during the past two and a half years, adding that the PTI had been offered an opportunity to join hands with the federal government to combat terrorism, as it had done in the past.

He also said that hundreds of billions had been allocated to the KP government under a special National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangement to combat terrorism.

“How many Safe City projects have been initiated in KP? How much money has been spent on strengthening the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD)?” he asked.

The prime minister elaborated that even if the PTI-led KP government had spent Rs80 billion on strengthening the police and other law enforcement agencies, they would have been better equipped to tackle security challenges. “But unfortunately, that did not happen,” he added.

He said the federal government had managed to put the national economy back on its feet, but acknowledged that the recovery process would be a long journey.

The prime minister recalled that the government had formed a committee comprising members of the PPP and PML-N to hold talks with the PTI.

“Both sides held negotiations for 48 hours. I was told that the draft had been finalised and would be signed within minutes, following approval from then-chief minister Sohail Afridi. However, the approval never came, and we are still waiting,” he said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz said the federal government was compelled to impose an emergency and governor’s rule, as it had no other option.

He emphasised that the Centre’s decision had been “timely”, warning that the consequences would have been severe had it been delayed.

The prime minister urged PML-N lawmakers from KP to prioritise the basic needs of the people in their constituencies, while putting long-term projects on hold for the time being.

“Focus on short-term welfare projects so that you can help turn people’s fortunes around within the next six months to a year,” he stressed.

PTI hits back at PM’s criticism

Meanwhile, the PTI hit back at the premier’s criticism, challenging the federal government to account for its own record instead of blaming the party for KP’s security and governance problems.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the prime minister had no moral authority to lecture the party on democracy and governance, alleging that the present political setup had come into power through electoral manipulation and political arrangements.

Waqas accused the federal government of shifting responsibility for the province’s worsening security situation onto the PTI provincial government. He alleged that the federal government had failed to provide the province with necessary resources and equipment for counterterrorism operations.

He also accused the Centre of focusing on political opposition rather than addressing security and governance issues, alleging that PTI leaders and workers had faced raids, arrests and intimidation.

He also challenged the premier to present a comprehensive account of his government’s four-year performance.

Less than a week after emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in the province, a joint sitting of parliament approved the federal government’s move amid a strong protest from the opposition.

The events of Oct 11 followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Federal ministers alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups and asserted that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

The Centre and the PTI have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied. It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Additional input from Ikram Junaidi.

article_html:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday criticised PTI’s governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, questioning whether the funds available to the now dysfunctional provincial government had been used transparently for the welfare and betterment of the people of the province.

His remarks came during a meeting of the PML-N’s parliamentary party from KP, held in Islamabad.

The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move had drawn criticism from the opposition, as well as Fazl, who had made efforts to reduce tensions between the federal and the KP governments.

Taking aim at the PTI, Prime Minister Shehbaz said: “They have been in power in KP for 13 years. Over these 13 years, they have raised countless slogans, delivered fiery speeches, held long marches and sit-ins, and made numerous promises.”

Recalling PTI’s promises to build hundreds of dams, generate hundreds of megawatts of solar power, and establish hospitals, universities and schools across the province, the prime minister questioned whether any of these pledges had been fulfilled during the party’s 13 years in power.

“How many universities have been established there? How many new hospitals have been built? How much has the healthcare system improved? What facilities have actually been provided to the people? And how much corruption has taken place in the process?” he asked.

The prime minister also questioned whether public funds had been utilised transparently for the welfare and betterment of the people of KP.

“From Peshawar to Kohistan and Hazara, and across the entire southern region of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the majority of people would tell you that the PTI government has done very little, if anything, to address their basic needs,” he said.

The premier maintained that by 2017-18, terrorist activities in the province had been brought to an end to “a considerable extent”.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was among the provinces that made the greatest sacrifices in the fight against terrorism,” he said.

The prime minister highlighted the heavy toll terrorism had taken on the country, saying around 80,000 people had lost their lives and Pakistan’s economy had suffered losses estimated at Rs15,000 billion.

He also praised former prime minister and PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif for his policies to combat terrorism following the 2014 Army Public School tragedy, in which more than 140 students and teachers were killed.

Turning to the PTI, the prime minister said the party had spent the past two and a half years engaged in long marches and protests.

“In 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping was scheduled to visit Pakistan. We made repeated efforts to persuade the party to call off its sit-in so that President Xi’s visit could proceed as planned, but it refused. As a result, the visit was postponed,” he said, recalling the 2014 D-Chowk protest.

He also criticised the PTI for allowing “brutal terrorists” from Afghanistan to settle in Swat.

“These were among the most painful and heartrending incidents that allowed terrorism to regain momentum,” he said.

The premier further said that thousands of civilians and security personnel had been martyred during the past two and a half years, adding that the PTI had been offered an opportunity to join hands with the federal government to combat terrorism, as it had done in the past.

He also said that hundreds of billions had been allocated to the KP government under a special National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangement to combat terrorism.

“How many Safe City projects have been initiated in KP? How much money has been spent on strengthening the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD)?” he asked.

The prime minister elaborated that even if the PTI-led KP government had spent Rs80 billion on strengthening the police and other law enforcement agencies, they would have been better equipped to tackle security challenges. “But unfortunately, that did not happen,” he added.

He said the federal government had managed to put the national economy back on its feet, but acknowledged that the recovery process would be a long journey.

The prime minister recalled that the government had formed a committee comprising members of the PPP and PML-N to hold talks with the PTI.

“Both sides held negotiations for 48 hours. I was told that the draft had been finalised and would be signed within minutes, following approval from then-chief minister Sohail Afridi. However, the approval never came, and we are still waiting,” he said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz said the federal government was compelled to impose an emergency and governor’s rule, as it had no other option.

He emphasised that the Centre’s decision had been “timely”, warning that the consequences would have been severe had it been delayed.

The prime minister urged PML-N lawmakers from KP to prioritise the basic needs of the people in their constituencies, while putting long-term projects on hold for the time being.

“Focus on short-term welfare projects so that you can help turn people’s fortunes around within the next six months to a year,” he stressed.

PTI hits back at PM’s criticism

Meanwhile, the PTI hit back at the premier’s criticism, challenging the federal government to account for its own record instead of blaming the party for KP’s security and governance problems.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the prime minister had no moral authority to lecture the party on democracy and governance, alleging that the present political setup had come into power through electoral manipulation and political arrangements.

Waqas accused the federal government of shifting responsibility for the province’s worsening security situation onto the PTI provincial government. He alleged that the federal government had failed to provide the province with necessary resources and equipment for counterterrorism operations.

He also accused the Centre of focusing on political opposition rather than addressing security and governance issues, alleging that PTI leaders and workers had faced raids, arrests and intimidation.

He also challenged the premier to present a comprehensive account of his government’s four-year performance.

Less than a week after emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in the province, a joint sitting of parliament approved the federal government’s move amid a strong protest from the opposition.

The events of Oct 11 followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Federal ministers alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups and asserted that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

The Centre and the PTI have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied. It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Additional input from Ikram Junaidi.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi tells Al Jazeera that a US effort to open dialogue with Iran is “a positive step”.

Tehran’s top diplomat says his country has studied a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance in high-level meetings.

“The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step,” he says, though he warns, “If Washington’s goal in sending this letter is to stir up discord, it would be yet another mistake to add to its previous ones.”

description: In an interview with Al Jazeera, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denies that there are any planned meetings...
article_text:
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denies that there are any planned meetings with US officials.

“What is being circulated in this regard is merely media speculation,” he explains. “We see no need to meet with the Americans at present. Our conditions are clear, and mediators are continuing their consultations regarding them.”

Araghchi adds that a decision on whether to hold direct or indirect talks with the US depends on Washington meeting Tehran’s conditions.

headline: Araghchi says Iran has not ruled out potential attacks
description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran has not ruled out the possibility of an attack against the...
article_text:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran has not ruled out the possibility of an attack against the country.

“We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war, and we are prepared for all scenarios,” Araghchi tells Al Jazeera. “We have upgraded our weaponry, addressed our vulnerabilities, and tested new arms; our forces are at the highest level of readiness.”

Acknowledging the effects of the US-imposed economic pressure on Iran, Araghchi says Iran “will not surrender”.

“We will continue to stand firm and resist, and we will overcome this difficult phase through our own capabilities,” he adds.

headline: Mansehra assistant commissioner injured as vehicle comes under attack in Nowshera
description: Hospital official says AC Adil Waseem is "stable"; search operation launched to trace attackers.
author: Umer Farooq, Ashfaq Yusufzai
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Mansehra Assistant Commissioner (AC) Adil Waseem was injured on Saturday when unknown gunmen opened fire at his official vehicle in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district, officials said.

Muhammad Asim, the spokesperson of Peshawar’s Lady Reading Hospital, said Waseem was “stable” and was receiving medical treatment.

Waseem came under attack in Nowshera’s Panah Kot area while on his way back from his native village Saleh Khana in the district, police officials in Nowshera said.

He sustained injuries and was immediately taken to the hospital.

According to Nowshera District Police Officer (DPO) Sonia Shamroz, the area was immediately cordoned off and a search operation was launched. She added that a team has been constituted to arrest those behind the attack.

DPO Shamroz further said a case has been registered and investigation into the incident was under way.

KP has been witnessing increased terrorist attacks and security challenges in recent years, including attacks on law enforcement personnel and officials.

According to a recent report by the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters.

KP and Balochistan remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

On Thursday night, a cop was martyred after terrorists attacked a police post in Bajaur district’s Barang tehsil.

Last week, four policemen, including a Counter-Terrorism Department official and a station house officer, were martyred while two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in the Karak district.

In December 2025, Miranshah AC Shah Wali was among four martyred after the official’s vehicle came under attack in Bannu. In July that year, Nawagai subdivision AC Faisal Ismail and four others lost their lives in an explosion targeting a government vehicle in Bajaur.

headline: New proposal shortens implementation of Iran’s plan to open Hormuz to 2 days, Araghchi says
description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with Qatari mediators have resulted in a shorter period required...
article_text:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with Qatari mediators have resulted in a shorter period required to implement Iran’s proposal to open the Strait of Hormuz.

“The Qatari side proposed shortening the implementation period of the Iranian proposal to five days. We have reached a proposal at this stage that reduces the implementation period to two days,” Araghchi tells Al Jazeera in an interview.

“Our conditions include lifting the sanctions imposed following the Islamabad memorandum and reducing US forces in the region. We demand the restoration of oil waivers and the release of all our frozen funds, including those held in Qatar,” he adds.

Tehran’s top diplomat says his country demands the recognition of shipping routes discussed by Iran and Oman in the Strait of Hormuz and the closure of other routes.

“Reopening the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with our conditions paves the way for the resumption of negotiations with Washington regarding outstanding issues,” he stresses.

Tehran’s top diplomat says his country demands the recognition of shipping routes discussed by Iran and Oman in the Strait of Hormuz and the closure of other routes.
“Reopening the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with our conditions paves the way for the resumption of negotiations with Washington regarding outstanding issues,” he stresses.

The Israeli military has carried out fresh airstrikes, an explosion and machine-gun fire across southern Lebanon, Anadolu reports citing the state-run National News Agency.

Israeli strikes and military operations have targeted several locations across southern Lebanon, including the districts of Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun, according to the news agency.

The attacks come despite a US-brokered framework agreement signed by Lebanon and Israel in June and renewed diplomatic efforts to address security disputes between the two sides.

headline: Sindh CM Murad blames city planners for 'ruining' Karachi
description: Chief minister says master plans of 14 cities completed; laments lack of mapping of utility infrastructure.
author: News Desk
article_text:
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Saturday blamed urban planners for “ruining” Karachi, adding that he saw the metropolis vastly expand and deteriorate firsthand while growing up in it.

In July 2025, a steering committee tasked with developing the Greater Karachi Regional Plan 2047 was informed that the new master plan of the country’s commercial capital would be ready within two years.

Addressing an event of the Sindh Master Plan Authority (SMPA) in Karachi, CM Murad said: “Making a master plan from scratch is easy. But considering Karachi’s deteriorated condition, it is a challenge for consultants, master planners and urban developers to fix those [conditions], and also for the executive bodies to implement the plan.”

CM Murad noted that SMPA, established under the Karachi Development Authority (KDA) in 1968, was formed to develop urban master plans for Sindh’s cities with recommendations from stakeholders.

The chief minister said 14 master plans had been completed, but plans for Karachi and Hyderabad were under development. However, a post by the CM House quoted him as saying that master plans for 17 cities were complete, with work on 14 in final stages.

Recalling that he grew up in Karachi and saw the metropolis’ expansion firsthand, Murad said, “I do not think any other city in the world has expanded as quickly as Karachi has, nor has any city in the world been ruined by planners as quickly as Karachi has.”

The chief minister, whose PPP has ruled Sindh for about 15 years, stressed that Karachi needed to be improved. He contended that from the 1960s to the 1980s, it was a “very well-planned” city which attracted foreign visitors.

Recalling an incident during the severe rains of 2020, Murad lamented that while travelling along a new dual-carriageway road from Yousuf Goth, he saw that people had set up shops along the side roads, the stormwater drains on either side of the main road and even on the median.

“The planners did a very good job, but … a lot of roads have been declared commercial in the city and, to give people a livelihood, they are allowed to set up shops on stormwater drains for very cheap rent,” he said.

“I request the help of all stakeholders in [solving] this issue. Unless the entire city comes together to make it better, then we will not be successful.”

CM Murad also regretted that on several occasions, development work faced challenges due to delays from utility service providers, including the water board.

He also pointed out the lack of mapping of utility infrastructure: “There is no mapping anywhere.”

Noting Karachi’s population of 25 million and how urban development work inconveniences Karachiites, the chief minister said that funds have been arranged to rework 143 roads, but the work had not started because of procurement issues, which he said, “take a lifetime, but that’s how things are”.

However, he stressed the importance of forums under SMPA to discuss urban planning and implementation.

“These types of forums, seminars and discussions will help us bring some improvement and right now, in every city … the mayors and divisional headquarters are all trying to emulate the development which has started in Karachi.”

headline: Iranian military's chief of staff warns 'continuously updating our target database'
description: Major General Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the General Staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, says Tehran is monitoring the US’...
article_text:
Major General Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the General Staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, says Tehran is monitoring the US’ movements and preparations using our full intelligence capabilities, and “continuously updating our target database”, according to a statement carried by the ISNA news agency.

“Should signs of a hostile act by the enemy be confirmed, the armed forces will not wait for the enemy to initiate their action before determining the timing and manner of our response. Our response will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations,“ he warns.

headline: Turkiye nominates veteran diplomat Sinirlioglu for role of UN chief
description: Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu has remained Turkiye's foreign minister and envoy to UN; currently serves as secretary general of Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
author: AFP
article_text:
Turkiye has nominated Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, secretary general of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), to be the next United Nations chief, a diplomatic source confirmed on Saturday.

The move came after a deadlock in the selection process, with the latest straw poll at the UN Security Council (UNSC) held on Friday returning an inconclusive outcome. Sinirlioglu serves in the OSCE, which describes itself as the world’s “largest regional security organisation” with 57 members.

Contacted by AFP, the Turkish diplomatic source confirmed that the nomination letter dated Oct 30 from Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan was submitted to the presidents of the UN General Assembly and the UNSC.

In the letter, published by Turkish media, Erdogan said the nomination reflected Ankara’s commitment to “effective multilateralism” at a time when “geopolitical divisions are deepening and trust between nations is diminishing”.

With more than four decades of experience in international relations and diplomacy, Sinirlioglu has held some of Turkiye’s highest diplomatic positions, including foreign minister and permanent representative to the UN, Erdogan said in the letter.

The choice of the next UN chief would be crucial in steering the international community towards “a more peaceful, just and sustainable future” amid mounting global challenges, he added.

The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on Dec 31.

Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 available in the UNSC, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided.

Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.

headline: Harmer, Rabada steer South Africa to series win over Australia
description: Australia were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the test world rankings for the first time since January 2016.
author: Reuters
article_text:
South Africa spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 and Kagiso Rabada became the fastest by balls bowled to reach 350 Test wickets as the hosts thumped Australia by 176 runs to clinch their three-match series 2-1 at Newlands on Saturday.

Chasing a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the Test world rankings for the first time since January 2016.

Australia had hopes of chasing down the total but lost two wickets in the first over of the final day and slumped to 62 for eight as their effort became a battle of survival that South Africa ended before tea.

There will be questions asked of this Australia side in the wake of the defeat, not least another poor batting display and the decision to bowl on the opening morning that left them batting last on a wearing wicket.

“The trend of this game was once you got yourself in there were runs to be had,” Australia captain Pat Cummins said. “But within the first hour the game was away from us and we did not give ourselves a chance.

“We are a really good side but playing tough opponents away from home is always difficult. We came here thinking we were good enough to win but we couldn’t do it.”

Hopes of victory evaporated in the first half hour as Rabada (3-39) removed the top three batters to take his tally to 350 Test wickets, taking 13,808 deliveries, fewer than compatriot Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan’s Waqar Younis (14,905).

After that Harmer came into his own, exploiting the conditions expertly to also claim a first 10-wicket haul in Tests with figures of 10-120 across the match.

Rabada removed opener Matt Renshaw (0), caught by wicket-keeper Ryan Rickelton down the leg side, and the struggling Marnus Labuschagne (4) leg before wicket in the first over of the innings.

He then had the dangerous Travis Head caught at gully by Marco Jansen to rock Australia early on.

First-innings centurion Josh Inglis (4) was run out attempting a quick single to compound Australia’s woes, and from there Harmer took the last six wickets.

Cummins (11 from 90 balls) and innings top-scorer Nathan Lyon (33 not out) delayed the inevitable with a ninth-wicket stand that lasted 17.2 overs, but Harmer trapped the former lbw and then bowled Josh Hazlewood to seal the win.

“It was just understanding what I needed to do, getting the ball in the right areas as often as I could, and playing with my pace and trajectories, the little nuances I have learnt along the way. It all worked out alright,” Harmer said.

“Today was a lot of fun, fielders around the bat and trying to get the win. That is the stuff of dreams for a spinner.”

The victory also keeps alive South Africa’s hopes of defending their World Test Championship title next year having beaten Australia at Lord’s in the 2025 decider.

headline: Iran targeted US air defenses then hit aircraft and buildings on Middle East bases: report
description: Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases across the Middle East targeted early-warning systems before hitting...
article_text:
Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases across the Middle East targeted early-warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage, according to an analysis by The Associated Press.

The AP has independently verified damage to US facilities using satellite imagery and speaking to four regional officials briefed on what was hit. The news outlet has found that more than 115 drone and missile strikes in August, claimed by Iran or pro-Iran militias, damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with American equipment.

The AP has found that Iran initially targeted aircraft hangars and air defence systems that detect incoming strikes, clearing the way for further attacks on warehouses, aircraft troop housing, hangars and other facilities.

Two regional officials say the US has moved many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf, including aircraft, air defence systems, communications systems and other equipment crucial to base operations.

headline: ECP notifies delimitation schedule for Quetta, Kharian cantonment boards after reclassification
description: Delimitation exercise for Quetta and Kharian will be carried out from November this year to January 2027.
author: Iftikhar A. Khan
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has notified delimitation schedules for the Quetta and Kharian cantonment boards following their reclassification by the federal government.

The federal government has reclassified the Quetta Cantonment Board from Class-II to Class-I and that in Punjab’s Kharian from Class-III to Class-II. The ECP has fixed the number of wards in Quetta at 10 and five in Kharian.

According to three notifications issued on Oct 29, the delimitation exercise for Quetta and Kharian will be carried out from November this year until January 2027.

Administrative arrangements, including the procurement of maps and training of committees and authorities, will be completed from Nov 2 to 4, and delimitation committees will prepare preliminary lists of wards from Nov 5 to 19, which will be published on Nov 20 to invite objections.

Objections can be filed before delimitation authorities from Nov 21 to Dec 20. The authorities will dispose of objections by Jan 5, 2027 and communicate decisions to committees by Jan 8. Final lists of wards will be published on Jan 13.

The ECP has appointed the Gujrat district election commissioner as the convener of the delimitation committee for Kharian, with the Kharian cantonment executive officer and Gujrat assistant election commissioner as members.

For Quetta, the Quetta East district election commissioner will act as convener, while the Quetta additional cantonment executive officer and Quetta East assistant election commissioner will serve as members.

The regional election commissioners for Gujranwala and Quetta have been appointed as delimitation authorities for the Kharian and Quetta cantonment boards, respectively, to decide objections.

The commission directed that officers appointed for delimitation shall not be transferred without its prior approval.

The issuance of the delimitation schedule follows the ECP’s fixation of a case on delay in the conduct of LG polls in cantonment boards across the country. The electoral body had directed its office to immediately prepare and submit a schedule for LG elections in cantonment boards for approval.

The case, initially fixed for Oct 28, could not be held and was finally fixed for Nov 10. Notices have been issued to the defence ministry secretary and the director general of the Military Lands and Cantonments Department.

In its meetings on Oct 5 and Oct 15 regarding the delay in LG polls in four provinces, Islamabad and cantonment boards, the ECP was informed that the entire delimitation process for cantonments had been completed and the commission is prepared to hold elections.

However, under Section 19D(2) of the Cantonments Act 2023, the federal government is required to submit a formal request to the ECP to hold these elections. The ECP noted that despite reminders and a letter from the chief election commissioner to the prime minister, the request has not been submitted.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has notified delimitation schedules for the Quetta and Kharian cantonment boards following their reclassification by the federal government.

The federal government has reclassified the Quetta Cantonment Board from Class-II to Class-I and that in Punjab’s Kharian from Class-III to Class-II. The ECP has fixed the number of wards in Quetta at 10 and five in Kharian.

According to three notifications issued on Oct 29, the delimitation exercise for Quetta and Kharian will be carried out from November this year until January 2027.

Administrative arrangements, including the procurement of maps and training of committees and authorities, will be completed from Nov 2 to 4, and delimitation committees will prepare preliminary lists of wards from Nov 5 to 19, which will be published on Nov 20 to invite objections.

Objections can be filed before delimitation authorities from Nov 21 to Dec 20. The authorities will dispose of objections by Jan 5, 2027 and communicate decisions to committees by Jan 8. Final lists of wards will be published on Jan 13.

The ECP has appointed the Gujrat district election commissioner as the convener of the delimitation committee for Kharian, with the Kharian cantonment executive officer and Gujrat assistant election commissioner as members.

For Quetta, the Quetta East district election commissioner will act as convener, while the Quetta additional cantonment executive officer and Quetta East assistant election commissioner will serve as members.

The regional election commissioners for Gujranwala and Quetta have been appointed as delimitation authorities for the Kharian and Quetta cantonment boards, respectively, to decide objections.

The commission directed that officers appointed for delimitation shall not be transferred without its prior approval.

The issuance of the delimitation schedule follows the ECP’s fixation of a case on delay in the conduct of LG polls in cantonment boards across the country. The electoral body had directed its office to immediately prepare and submit a schedule for LG elections in cantonment boards for approval.

The case, initially fixed for Oct 28, could not be held and was finally fixed for Nov 10. Notices have been issued to the defence ministry secretary and the director general of the Military Lands and Cantonments Department.

In its meetings on Oct 5 and Oct 15 regarding the delay in LG polls in four provinces, Islamabad and cantonment boards, the ECP was informed that the entire delimitation process for cantonments had been completed and the commission is prepared to hold elections.

However, under Section 19D(2) of the Cantonments Act 2023, the federal government is required to submit a formal request to the ECP to hold these elections. The ECP noted that despite reminders and a letter from the chief election commissioner to the prime minister, the request has not been submitted.

headline: India opposition parties hold mock impeachment of poll chief
description: Senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi says the opposition resorted to the symbolic exercise as they “have nowhere else to go”.
author: AFP
article_text:
India’s political opposition staged a symbolic impeachment of the election commissioner on Saturday to protest against a revision of voter lists that they say could unfairly benefit the ruling party.

The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world’s largest democracy over the last month.

The election commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Both the commission and the BJP deny the allegations.

On Saturday, opposition parties gathered at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in the capital, New Delhi, re-enacting a parliamentary session. They held mock impeachment proceedings, which have no constitutional or legal force, against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

“The motion we have brought forward today is aimed at safeguarding the dignity of a constitutional institution,” Kharge said. “Our intention is for the election commission to function impartially, in line with the spirit of the constitution.”

Under the constitution, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a parliamentary process requiring a special majority.

Senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the opposition had resorted to the symbolic exercise as they “have nowhere else to go”.

“We have no other option. Every single institution … is closed for us,” Gandhi said.

The event came a day before a major opposition rally in Delhi backed by the Cockroach Janta Party, an online youth-led movement that also supports the campaign against the voter-roll revision.

Home Minister Amit Shah said the BJP was ready to hold a special session of parliament to discuss the revision.

“But they (the opposition) have no intention of speaking there. They refuse to let the parliament function. Instead, they just create a ruckus,” he said.

headline: 1 dead, over 14 injured during stampede at TikToker's mehndi ceremony in Sialkot
description: TikTok influencer, known as “Mr Patlu”, was also holding a prize-distribution event at a cricket ground.
author: Abid Mahmood
article_text:
NAROWAL: A stampede at a mehndi (henna) ceremony and prize-distribution event for a TikTok influencer in Sialkot left one person dead and more than 14 others injured last night, officials said on Saturday.

The mehndi ceremony and prize-distribution event for Muhammad Ansar Jatt, a popular TikToker from Sialkot district known as “Mr Patlu”, was scheduled for Saturday night at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road.

During the mehndi ceremony, motorcycles and a car were to be awarded to attendees through a lucky draw. Hundreds of followers from various cities across Punjab had gathered outside the ground well before the scheduled time to attend the event.

As event organisers opened the stadium gates to allow the attendees in, a stampede ensued and many fell to the ground. Those caught in the pushing and shoving or trampled underfoot could be heard screaming and crying out.

Attendees began moving those injured in the stampede to nearby clinics and private hospitals on their own initiative, while rescue teams also immediately arrived at the scene upon receiving reports.

Police and Rescue 1122 personnel conducted a joint rescue operation and transported the injured to Allama Iqbal Memorial Teaching Hospital. Most of the individuals were discharged after receiving first aid, while others remained under medical care.

Among the injured, 30-year-old Muhammad Aqeel passed away while being transported to the hospital due to his critical condition.

According to a rescue spokesperson, the other 14 injured persons comprised men aged between 22 and 51 years. They hailed from various districts, including Narowal, Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Khanewal, Okara, Sialkot, Gujrat and Bahawalpur.

However, Sialkot residents Muhammad Asif and Aamir Ali stated that more than 40 people were injured in the stampede, explaining that before the rescue teams arrived, attendees had taken several injured to nearby private hospitals and clinics for first aid on their own.

Sialkot District Emergency Officer Engineer Naveed Iqbal said the rescue service had not been informed in advance about the large gathering planned at the cricket ground. He added that four ambulances and one motorcycle ambulance participated in the rescue operation.

Following the incident, Sialkot District Police Officer (DPO) Dost Muhammad had also reached the site, accompanied by a large police contingent and the Elite Force.

Acting on the DPO’s instructions, the police took charge of security arrangements, brought the crowd under control, and ensured that rescue operations could proceed without interruption.

Speaking to Dawn, DPO Muhammad criticised the event organisers for opening the stadium gates ahead of schedule. The retired captain noted that granting permission for such an event fell under the purview of the district administration.

Dawn has reached out to Sialkot Deputy Commissioner Awais Mushtaq for comment.

The DPO emphasised that the protection of the lives and property of citizens remains the police’s top priority. All aspects of the incident will be examined and appropriate legal action will be taken, he asserted.

Following the incident, Sialkot District Police Officer (DPO) Dost Muhammad had also reached the site, accompanied by a large police contingent and the Elite Force.

Acting on the DPO’s instructions, the police took charge of security arrangements, brought the crowd under control, and ensured that rescue operations could proceed without interruption.

Speaking to Dawn, DPO Muhammad criticised the event organisers for opening the stadium gates ahead of schedule. The retired captain noted that granting permission for such an event fell under the purview of the district administration.

Dawn has reached out to Sialkot Deputy Commissioner Awais Mushtaq for comment.

The DPO emphasised that the protection of the lives and property of citizens remains the police’s top priority. All aspects of the incident will be examined and appropriate legal action will be taken, he asserted.
